scope.included: apps/*, apps/mcp-servers/*, packages/* (pnpm workspace members only - i.e. dirs with a package.json), plus 13 scripts/* modules proven to be imported by >=3 other scripts/ files
scope.excludedRationale: scripts/ (736 source files total) was NOT fully graphed as individual nodes per-file - only genuinely shared scripts/lib-style modules (in-degree >=3 within scripts/) were added as nodes, consistent with the brief's 'anything imported by multiple other things does [need a node]' rule. tools/agent-relationship-graph, tools/config-files, tools/framework-master-graph, tests/, e2e/, test-suite/ were not graphed as nodes (no package.json, not proven to be widely-imported modules) but were grep-checked as CONSUMERS of the zero-fan-in packages list.

knownExclusions: packages/agent/srcs/ and packages/agent/srcsrc/ (3 files total) were excluded from the graph after being identified as orphaned duplicate trees NOT covered by packages/agent/tsconfig.json's include:['src/**/*'] - see findings.
*.d.ts, *.test.*, *.spec.*, __tests__/, __mocks__/, node_modules/, dist/, build/, .next/, coverage/ excluded from file walk.
caveats: No node_modules is installed in this worktree, so neither madge nor TypeScript could perform real module resolution against tsconfig paths or package 'exports' maps. All bare-specifier (package-name) edges below were recovered by regexing import/require/export-from/dynamic-import string literals and matching them against the 91 workspace package names declared in package.json files - this finds real source-level references but cannot detect indirect usage (e.g. a type consumed only via tsconfig 'types' array or triple-slash reference, or a package used only as a CLI 'bin' at runtime).

'declared but never imported' and 'fan-in = 0' findings are therefore upper-bound estimates of dead coupling, not proof of dead code - they mean 'no source-level import statement referencing this package name was found by regex across apps/*, packages/*, and a scripts/tests/tools sweep', not 'nothing on disk ever touches this package'.

An initial attempt to run madge directly on scripts/ as its own root produced misleadingly large numbers (e.g. '43 scripts import apps/api/src/guards/secure-auth.guard.ts') because madge followed a handful of relative imports OUT of scripts/ into apps/api and then kept walking apps/api's own internal file graph, attributing apps/api's internal edges to the scripts/ root. Filtering to edges whose SOURCE file is actually under scripts/ reduced this to 15 real scripts/->package|app crossings across 12 distinct scripts (see scriptToPackageCrossings). This is called out explicitly because it is exactly the kind of tool-artifact that looks like a structural finding but isn't.
